extra.message: The `expr` query parameter is passed directly to `eval()`. Although `__builtins__` is emptied, Python expression evaluation on attacker-controlled input is still exploitable (e.g. traversing `().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()` to reach `os`/`subprocess` and achieve remote code execution), and at minimum allows resource-exhaustion expressions. Never evaluate untrusted input.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: `pickle.loads()` is called on the raw HTTP request body (or the base64-decoded `blob` query parameter). Python pickle deserialization executes arbitrary code via `__reduce__`, so any client that can reach this endpoint gains remote code execution on the payroll server.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: The `fragment` query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 `Template(...)` string and rendered. This is server-side template injection: the attacker controls template syntax and can reach Python objects through Jinja2's sandbox-less default environment (e.g. `{{ cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen('id').read() }}`), giving remote code execution. The rendered result is also returned as `text/html`, producing reflected XSS.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: The `name` query parameter is joined onto `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` with no canonicalisation, confinement check, or allowlist, and the request body is then written to that path with `write_bytes()`. A value such as `name=../../hr_payroll/settings.py` (or an absolute path, which `pathlib` `/` honours) lets an attacker write arbitrary files anywhere the process can write, including overwriting application source for remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: The `ref` query parameter is interpolated into the export file path (`BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json"`) without normalisation or confinement, so `ref=../../../tmp/evil` writes outside the intended directory. The written content also embeds attacker-supplied SSN and card values in cleartext on disk.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: The JSON request body (`filter`, or the whole payload) is passed unvalidated as the MongoDB query document to `find_one()`. An attacker can inject query operators such as `{"$ne": null}`, `{"$gt": ""}` or `{"$where": "..."}` to bypass intended filtering and read arbitrary records from the `ops.records` collection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The privilege decision is made from the client-supplied `ops_badge` cookie or `x-ops-badge` header. Any caller can send `ops_badge=lead` to be granted the elevated lane with full payroll and casework access. Authorization must derive from authenticated server-side identity and policy state, never from a request-controlled value.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: Both the debit `amount` and the ledger `state` (approval status) are taken directly from the request body/query string and applied to the ledger with no server-side validation against the `limit`. A caller can post a negative amount to credit the balance or set `state=approved` to self-approve a payroll adjustment.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: Authentication verifiers for the `north` and `south` handles are hardcoded 4-digit values in source (`{"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}`). Anyone with source or repository access authenticates directly, the secrets cannot be rotated, and the 4-digit space is trivially brute-forced. The distinct 404/403 responses additionally allow handle enumeration.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: This verifier-check endpoint has no rate limiting, throttling, attempt counter, or lockout — neither in the view, in `_wrk_gate`, nor in any project middleware (`hr_payroll/settings.py` MIDDLEWARE contains no throttling layer). cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The `lane` query parameter is passed straight to `redirect()` with no allowlist or same-host validation, so `?lane=https://evil.example/login` issues a 302 to an attacker-controlled site. This enables phishing that appears to originate from the HR portal domain.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: The full compensation-intake request body and the raw `Authorization` header are written to the application log at WARNING level. cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The exception string (which embeds the absolute server path `BASE_EXPORT_DIR`) and the exception class name are returned to the client in the JSON error response. This leaks filesystem layout and internal implementation details useful for building path-traversal and RCE payloads.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The error response returns the raw exception text containing the absolute `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` server path plus the exception class name, disclosing internal filesystem structure to unauthenticated-to-the-app callers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The request's `Origin` header is reflected verbatim into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` while `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` is set to `true`. Any website can therefore issue authenticated cross-origin requests to this endpoint with the victim's session cookies and read the responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The response explicitly disables browser protection mechanisms by sending `X-XSS-Protection: 0` and an empty `Content-Security-Policy`. cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure

extra.message: `set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker)` is called without `httponly=True`, `secure=True`, or `samesite`, and the value comes straight from the `marker` query parameter. cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

extra.message: A nonce/code is generated with `random.choice()`, which is backed by the deterministic, non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister. Observing a modest number of issued codes lets an attacker recover the generator state and predict all subsequent nonces. Use `secrets.choice`/`secrets.token_urlsafe` for security tokens. The attacker-controlled `length` is also unbounded, allowing memory/CPU exhaustion.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: `ssl._create_unverified_context()` is used for the outbound HTTPS call to the partner endpoint, disabling certificate and hostname verification. Any network-position attacker can transparently man-in-the-middle the payroll partner connection, reading and rewriting the traffic.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: This diagnostic route is unconditionally enabled (`trace_on = True`, no `settings.DEBUG` guard) and returns internal runtime configuration — the `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` and the absolute `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` filesystem path — to callers in production.

cwe: CWE-489: Active Debug Code

extra.message: `DEBUG` defaults to True when the `DEBUG` environment variable is unset, so a deployment that forgets to set it runs with Django's debug mode active: unhandled exceptions render full tracebacks including local variables, settings, and SQL. It also transitively disables `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`/`CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE` (lines 130-132) and exposes MEDIA_ROOT/STATIC_ROOT via `hr_payroll/urls.py:19-21`. cwe: CWE-489: Active Debug Code

extra.message: `SECRET_KEY` falls back to the hardcoded literal `'django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-in-production'` when the environment variable is absent. This key signs session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens; with a value published in source an attacker can forge sessions and password-reset links for any account, including HR admins.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The PostgreSQL password defaults to the hardcoded literal `'hrpayroll123'` (with user/database names also defaulting to `hrpayroll`). Any deployment that does not set `DB_PASSWORD` is reachable with credentials published in the repository, exposing the full payroll and PII database.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: `policy_detail` fetches any `Policy` by primary key with only `@login_required` and never checks `policy.audience` against the caller's role, unlike `policy_list` (lines 16-21) which restricts manager/HR-only policies. A plain employee can read manager- or HR-restricted policy content by walking `/policies/<pk>/`. The authorization decision must be applied on the authoritative object read, not only in the listing view.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: The login endpoint uses Django's stock `LoginView` with no rate limiting, attempt counter, or account lockout. `hr_payroll/settings.py` MIDDLEWARE (lines 37-45) contains no throttling middleware and there is no gateway/decorator layer anywhere in the request path, so credentials for HR-admin accounts can be brute-forced without restriction. The same applies to `password_reset/` on line 8.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Authentication events are never written to the application's audit trail. The project defines `AuditLog.ACTION_LOGIN`/`ACTION_LOGOUT` and an `audit.utils.log_action` helper, but the stock `LoginView`/`LogoutView` are wired in with no signal receiver, middleware, or view wrapper that records successful logins, failed login attempts, or logouts (no `ACTION_LOGIN` producer exists anywhere in the codebase). Credential-stuffing and successful account takeover therefore leave no durable security event for detection or forensics.

cwe: CWE-778: Insufficient Logging

extra.message: `_require_api_key`/`_api_auth` return `None` on an invalid or inactive API key and each API view then returns a bare 401/403 without calling `audit.utils.log_action`. No API-key authentication failure, and no API authorization failure (`api_employees` line 85, `api_compensation` line 131, `api_documents` line 152), produces an audit record, even though `AuditLog.ACTION_FAILED_ACCESS` exists and is used by the HTML views. API-key guessing and unauthorized access attempts against payroll and document data are therefore invisible.

cwe: CWE-778: Insufficient Logging

extra.message: API-key creation/deletion and webhook endpoint creation/deletion are performed with no `log_action` call, unlike every other privileged mutation in the codebase. Credential lifecycle events for the keys that grant programmatic access to employee, compensation, and document data leave no audit record, so an HR-admin account takeover that mints a persistent API key is untraceable.

cwe: CWE-778: Insufficient Logging

extra.message: `comp_request_hr_approve` mutates state (final HR approval of a salary change, which the `process_effective_compensation` command later turns into a real compensation record) on any request method, including GET — there is no `if request.method == 'POST'` guard, and the template links to it with a plain `` (templates/compensation/comp_request_detail.html:37). The same flaw affects `comp_request_manager_approve` (line 118) and `comp_request_submit` (line 96).

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

extra.message: `task_waive` changes an onboarding task to WAIVED with no `request.method` check, so it executes on GET and bypasses CSRF protection entirely (CSRF middleware only validates unsafe methods). `task_approve` (line 64) and `task_reject` (line 87) have the same flaw and are linked as plain anchors in templates/employees/pending_approvals.html:17-18, so a single crafted image tag loaded by an HR admin or manager can approve or waive compliance tasks.

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

extra.message: `employee_edit` is reachable by a plain employee for their own profile (`_can_edit_employee`, line 50) and writes `employment_status` straight from POST data with no role gate and no validation against `STATUS_CHOICES`. cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: `log_action` takes the audit-record source IP from the client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` header whenever it is present, with no trusted-proxy check and no `USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST`/proxy configuration in settings.
